query: What are systematic failure modes of provenance/interpretability tools for large models and diffusion systems, and how can we benchmark when provenance metrics are reliable?

response.query: What are systematic failure modes of provenance/interpretability tools for large models and diffusion systems, and how can we benchmark when provenance metrics are reliable?
response.answer: Systematic failure modes of provenance/interpretability tools for large models include overfitting to training data and lack of generalizability. Benchmarking reliability involves cross-validation and real-world performance testing. Simple, consistent metrics often fail to capture complex model behaviors.

results.title: Colloquium
results.content: Polarization tomography is a valuable method for investigating the structure of magnetic fields in the interstellar medium. By combining polarization measurements with stellar distances, we can disentangle contributions from multiple intervening structures and reconstruct the plane-of-sky magnetic field at different depths along the line of sight. By mediating gas cooling, enabling molecule formation, and absorbing and re-emitting stellar radiation in far-infrared and Sub-mm regimes, dust serves as an essential tracer of the physical conditions, offering insights into the interplay of stars, dust and the ISM. With the help of multi-wavelength observations, it is possible to study the different components of the ISM and their relations in a spatially resolved manner across nearby galaxies, on scales of few hundreds to kiloparsecs. I will show that both young and evolved stellar popluations contribute to dust heating, and examine how dust content related to the gas and metals in the ISM through dust-to-gas and dust-to-metal ratios.
